newsitem.title: USA: Kmart Corp CEO calls estimates reasonable.
newsitem.headline: Kmart Corp CEO calls estimates reasonable.

text.p: Kmart Corp chairman, president and chief executive officer Floyd Hall said Wednesday that analysts' fourth quarter and fiscal year estimates of $0.34 and $0.35 respectively are "reasonable".

In last year's fourth quarter Kmart reported a loss of $0.91 a share on sales of $10.5 billion, including a charge of $0.85 a share related to Builders Square. Builders Square is a home improvement retailer owned by Kmart.
In the prior fiscal year Kmart reported a loss of $1.25 a share on sales of $34.4 billion.
Kmart is looking at a 3.5 percent to five percent increase in same-store sales for the holiday period, Hall said.
Although Hall said a six to seven percent same-store range is achievable, he did not want to sacrifice profits to boost that figure.
Kmart, which reported better than expected third quarter results earlier today, is trying to turn around its sagging operations and has introduced what it calls the "pantry concept."
Kmart's pantry concept is aimed at increasing store traffic and sales by devoting store space to lower profit margin consumer staples, such as diapers and household chemicals.
Hall expects the lower profit margins to be offset by greater sales and increased inventory turnover.
Regarding the status of the company's turnaround, Hall said Kmart is at "5-1/2 to six" on a scale of one to 10 with some departments operating better than others.
Achieving the high end of the scale would mean keeping stores better stocked with the goods in each department aimed at a carefully researched customer segment, Hall said.

Hall declined to say what departments in the 2,143 store chain are lagging, but did say that men's apparel exceeded the overall growth rate. Apparel sales have met the company's goals, Hall said, citing the higher quality of products over past offerings.
